{{Short description|Extinct language of Brazil}}{{Cleanup lang|date=February 2025|iso=uam}}{{Infobox language | name = Uamué | nativename = Aticum, Umã | states = [[Brazil]] | region = [[Floresta, Pernambuco]] | ethnicity = [[Atikum people]] | extinct = after 1961 | map = File:Atikum e Pankará.png | mapcaption = Map of Atikum territory in [[Carnaubeira da Penha]], eastern Brazil | familycolor = American | family = [[Unclassified language|unclassified]] ([[Kariri languages|Kariri]]?) | iso3 = uam | glotto = uamu1236 | glottorefname = Uamué | mapsize = 250px }} '''Uamué''' (Wamoe), {{a.k.a.}} '''Huamoé''', '''Uman''', or '''Atikum''', is an extinct language of Brazil that is too poorly attested to classify. The [[Pankararú language]] was historically spoken just to the south. It is also spelled ''Huamuê, Huamoi, Uame, Wamoé''. Alternate names are ''Umã'' and ''Aticum'' (''Atikum, Araticum''). There has been speculation that Huamoé was a [[Kariri languages|Kariri language]]. Today, the Atikum only preserve some of their language in the context of nature (e. g. {{Lang|uam|toê}} 'fire' and {{Lang|uam|sarapó}} 'large edible snake') and have entirely switched to Portuguese.{{Cite web |title=Atikum - Indigenous Peoples in Brazil |url=https://pib.socioambiental.org/en/Povo:Atikum |access-date=2025-03-20 |website=pib.socioambiental.org}}{{Cite book |last=Siqueira |first=Baptista |url=https://etnolinguistica.wdfiles.com/local--files/biblio%3Asiqueira-1978-cariris/Siqueira_1978_OsCaririsDoNordeste.pdf |title=Os Cariris do Nordeste |date=1978 |publisher=Editora Cátedra |location=Rio de Janeiro |language=pt}} ==Vocabulary== ===Pompeu (1958)=== Language variety spoken by the Indians of the [[Serra Negra Biological Reserve|Serra Negra]] in [[Pernambuco]], recorded in [[Brejo dos Padres]]:Pompeu Sobrinho, Thomaz. 1958.
